papers.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
papers.abstract: Post-hoc image explanations usually show where a model looks using spatial heatmaps or indicate which channels matter using global channel scores. These separate views are limiting for multispectral data because channel relevance is often spatially localized and physically meaningful. We introduce Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a full-grid attribution method overposition-channel players(g,c). For each spatial position, SSI fixes the observed surrounding context, defines aconditional gameover the channels at that position, and applies theShapley valueto this local game. The result is a fullspectral-spatial attributionmatrix rather than a single heatmap or a global channel ranking. SSI has a clear local interpretation. It satisfies Shapley fairness within each position, and aggregating its channel attributions exactly recovers the position-levelcontextual contrastobtained by replacing that position with the baseline. SSI also differs from context-averagedOwen-style hierarchical accounting, which uses the same position-channel grouping but averages over external spatial coalitions. On HLS Burn Scar, SSI outperforms anMC-Owen estimatoracross retained attribution metrics while using only about 6% of its evaluation budget. Across CUB-200, EuroSAT, and HLS Burn Scar under both per-channel mean and zero baselines, SSI achieves the best joint deletion and insertion AUC over dense, flat, and rank-1 baselines, yields the strongest spectral hit rates and channel deletion, and leads spatial localization on both annotated datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/AtheavenMa/Spectral-Spatial-Interpretation.

papers.title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
papers.abstract: Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks often emphasize final task success while providing limited assessment of intermediateexecution validity. Yet real-world business operations require agents to navigate extensive, potentially outdated or conflicting policies while satisfying critical constraints throughout execution. These requirements are particularly consequential in high-stakes domains such as payments, where intermediate violations can incur financial losses or regulatory consequences regardless of the final outcome. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduceBizBench, amulti-turn benchmarkgrounded in real-world procedures from a leading payments company. Itsexecutable environmentintegrates 789 knowledge documents and 601 discoverablebusiness tools, with consistent policies, states, and tool behavior. The benchmark comprises 50 tasks involvingresource constraints,temporal dependencies, prior commitments, and conflicting or outdated guidance. Each task is validated through reference execution, while deterministic checks assess both goal attainment andexecution validitywithout prescribing a single solution path. Experiments reveal substantial limitations even among frontier models: Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol achievestrict successrates of only 64.0% and 61.3%, respectively. For Qwen3.8-27B, goal attainment reaches 42.0%, butstrict successdrops to 32.7%, demonstrating how outcome-based evaluation can mask invalid execution. Beyond success rates, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash averages 191.3tool callsper run, approximately 70% more than reference executions, revealing substantial execution overhead. Overall,BizBenchestablishes a testbed for evaluating and advancinglong-horizon agentsbeyond task completion, toward reliable and constraint-compliant execution in complex business environments.

papers.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
papers.abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allowsin-context learning(ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3)physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5)long-horizon preservationof progress. Second, we study the agentic harness forembodied control. We identify thatclose-loop coordinationbetween a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., π0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

papers.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
papers.abstract: Asstreaming video generationadvances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. We introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark forinteractive streaming video generationspanning five tasks:avatar dialogue,avatar performance,world generation,instruction editing, andreference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution,state consistency, visual fidelity, andaudiovisual coordination, instantiated through ten task-specific metrics on a 0-100 scale. Evaluating 37 distinct models across 300 test cases, we find that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustainedstate consistency. In particular, request execution remains challenging: the highest task-specific scores are 36.90 for Following among seven avatar-performance models, 25.93 for Following in text-conditionedworld generation, and 15.00 for Edit Success among three reported reference-editing models. These findings identify reliable request execution under timing and preservation constraints as a central challenge for advancingomni-modal real-time interactive systems. The leaderboard is available at https://streameval.ai

papers.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
papers.abstract: Brain encodingmodels aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones. Using neural data to train large models from scratch or fully fine-tune them after task-pretraining has proven difficult because neural data is costly and limited. We show thatparameter-efficient fine-tuning(PEFT) enables us to effectively adapt very large pretrained backbones forbrain encodingwith a small number of trainable parameters. To make it computationally practical, we exploit the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in a single pass instead of using sliding windows, significantly reducing feature-extraction cost. This enables efficient fine-tuning ofmultimodal backboneswith up to 104B parameters, the largest model adapted forbrain encodingto our knowledge. Trained with alow-rank adapter(LoRA) and a lightweight readout, our approach consistently improvesbrain encodingperformance across nine diversemultimodal backbones. On the same Qwen3-Omni backbone as the prior state-of-the-art (SoTA), our method BrainLoRAachieves the best published performance on the Algonauts 2025 Challenge. We also show the adaptedmultimodal backbonesremain interpretable: modality attribution recovers the canonical sensory topography that prior work often obtains by construction from separate unimodal encoders, and neural adaptation increases the contribution of audio inputs andcross-modal mixingwithin the backbone. To scale out the number of adapted models, we develop amulti-LoRA kernelthat accelerates joint training of multipleLoRAs on a shared backbone. This enables an ensemble of 200+ adapted models that ranks first on the public Algonauts post-challenge leaderboard at the time of writing. Together, our results highlightPEFTas an efficient and powerful paradigm forbrain encoding.

papers.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
papers.abstract: Existingvision-language models(VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception. In this report, we present WeVisOne-VL (WeChat Vision All-in-One), a powerful VLM that unifies object-level andpixel-level perceptionthroughstructured next-token prediction. It supports multiple visual tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting, enabling localization at any user-specific granularity, from points and boxes to masks and alpha mattes. Architecturally, we integrate a lightweightpixel decoderinto the VLM via a special<OBJ> tokento generate instance-level pixel outputs. We train the model with a three-stagecurriculum SFTfollowed bymixed-task RL. Across over 30 benchmarks, WeVisOne-VL demonstrates leading performance on both object-level and pixel-level tasks, while maintaining robust rejection forobject-absent queries. By releasing WeVisOne-VL to the open-source community, we hope to advance VLMs from broad visual understanding toward truly reliable perception systems for real-world deployment.

papers.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
papers.abstract: Moving from controllable videos to genuinely playable worlds requires persistent world state, executable game rules, and low-latency interaction. We outline a roadmap for the next generation of Matrix-Game that separates game execution from visual generation through anexecutable game harness, and introduce Matrix-Game 4.0 as the first system built on this design. A lightweight game engine maintains world state and executes interaction rules, amultimodal coding agenttranslates player ideas into game code anddynamic scene captions, and a renderer based onautoregressive video modeltransforms engine-renderedlow-poly proxiesinto detailed visuals, conditioned on dynamic captions andmemory references. This framework provides continuous guidance for visual generation and enables natural-language creation and modification of scenes and gameplay. Our renderer is trained on aligned low-poly and high-fidelity video pairs and distilled into acausal generatorthat generates in four-frame chunks with one or twodenoising steps. Together with targeted inference optimizations, Matrix-Game 4.0 enables 480p, 60 FPS gameplay on a single NVIDIA RTX5090 with a key-press-to-display latency of 112ms. Single-step generation achieves 83FPS steady-state throughput with 18.2GiB of peak GPU memory usage. With fixed prompts, steady-state throughput also reaches 67FPS on an RTX5080 and 58FPS on an RTX5070Ti. We demonstrate customizable shooter and driving games with engine-enforced mechanics, and release code, model weights, and low-poly game assets to support research and creation of playable game worlds.

papers.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
papers.abstract: Reconstructing human activity fromegocentric videorequires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, andhand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. Achieving this coherence requires bothjoint reconstructionand aligned supervision, yet existing methods and datasets offer limited support for either. We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking. Central to EgoXperience is an automatic annotation engine, EgoX-Engine, that couples geometrically verifiedobject trackingwithSLAM-based world alignment, yielding consistent supervision for the camera, scene, hands, and objects. This yields EgoX-Data-6M, a 50-hour dataset of task-driven manipulation and locomotion within and across indoor and outdoor environments, with second-level task captions. We carefully select one hour across these activity categories as EgoX-Bench to evaluatejoint reconstruction. To translate this supervision into reconstruction, we introduce EgoX, trained with EgoX-Data-6M and complementary annotations from additional public datasets. Given monocularegocentric videoand first-frame object masks, our model achieves joint metric reconstruction of the camera, scene, hands, and objects in a sharedworld coordinate framewith a single forward pass. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance acrossscene estimationand world-space hand-object pose recovery. Against the strongest evaluated baselines, EgoX reduces camera, hand, and depth errors by 68.9%, 65.6%, and 42.9%, and improves object pose scores by 28.0%.

papers.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
papers.abstract: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couplesinstruction-guided image editingwith controllable generation of reusableRGBA layers. At its core,In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modelingjointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we proposeCompositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurateRGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.

papers.title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
papers.abstract: A login screen that appears after a tap on Sign in is expected; the same screen after a tap on View order is an attack. For GUI agents, safety is therefore a property of the transition rather than of the screen, and a monitor that inspects only screens can be defeated by reusing a legitimate one. Judging a transition requires an expectation of what should have followed the action. ExistingGUI world models provide one, but they output it as text, code, or images, so checking it against the observed screen requires a second model to judge the two. We argue that a world model meant forverificationshould instead predict in the space in which observations are encoded, and presentLGWM, adecoder-free,action-conditioned world modelthat predicts the representation of the next screen directly, trained without semantic annotation on 1.85M real GUI transitions.Verificationreduces to avector comparison, and the same signal reveals whether a mismatch is harmful. We evaluate onRSWT-BENCH, a diagnostic where each credential screen appears under both a legitimate and a hijacked transition, so detectors that see only the screen are at chance by construction. The training-free score reaches 0.987AUCat 17 ms per decision, on par with the strongest closed-source VLMs and about tenAUCpoints above generativeGUI world models at over three orders of magnitude lower latency. The residual direction reaches 0.953AUCat separating harmful from benign violations, where prompted VLMs are near chance. Further analyses show that the prediction is a usable future state rather than an anomaly score. World models have mostly served as simulators or planners; our results point to a third role,verification, for which predicting inrepresentation spaceis the natural design.

papers.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
papers.abstract: Humanegocentric experienceoffers a rich foundation for learning how the world is organized and how it changes through interaction. Realizing this potential at scale requires turning growing volumes of recordings into learning resources that connect scene structure, object semantics, and interaction histories across viewpoints and time, while reducing dependence on costly manual annotation. We introduce HOLI-WORLD, an integrated ecosystem connecting experience capture,world representation,automated data construction, model learning, and independent evaluation. To sup- port learning at scale, HOLIWORLD-Foundry combines complementary static anddynamic perceptionto automatically constructworld recordsthat connect persistent scene structure and evolving object states with interaction histories and supporting observations. HOLIWORLD-Data organizes these records from approximately 100 self-collected scenes into grounded learning resources, including approximately 80K QA pairs used to trainHOLIWORLD-VL-4B. Independent human annotations of heldout recordings formHOLIWORLD-Bench, supporting evaluation of both annotation quality and learned spatial and temporal understanding. Experiments on ScanNet, ScanNet++, Aria Digital Twin, andHOLIWORLD-Benchdemonstrate strong performance instatic perceptionand dynamic tracking, while training on HOLIWORLD-Data substantially improvesHOLIWORLD-VL-4B's spatial andtemporal reasoningon HOLI- WORLD-Bench and EgoDynamic4D. HOLIWORLD provides a practical foundation for expanding learning resources from the continuous flow of human experience and advancing machine understanding of the dynamic world.

papers.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
papers.abstract: Cinematic video generation requires both temporal inference from limited inputs (i.e., sparse rather than frame-by-frame guidance) and factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera.Multimodal large language models(MLLMs) offer useful priors for both capabilities, but their representations are not automatically actionable for video generation: aVideo Diffusion Transformer(DiT) may bypass them through native conditioning pathways, and using them does not ensure either factor-aware control or generation-compatible temporal prediction. We propose Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL), which establishes effectiveMLLMlatent use as a shared prerequisite and then targets the two capabilities with complementary learning signals. First,latent-only generator groundingtrains theDiTwith a frozenMLLMand connector, strengthening theDiT's use ofMLLMlatents for generation. Second, for factor-aware control, paired videos specify a target-factor change and non-target preservation, andfactor-span replacementtrains theDiTto realize this relationship in its output. Third, for temporal inference, text-only and text-plus-complete-video observations share a video target, and the trainedDiTis then frozen while theMLLMand connector are optimized through it. This final stage trains limited-input representations for generation while retaining complete-observation reconstruction as a complementary training mode. Extensive experiments demonstrate our consistently better performance on three cinematic video generation tasks (i.e.,sparse-to-video,factor-aware editing, andmulti-shot generation) over baselines and validate FAPL's contributions toMLLMfeature use, temporal control, and factor coordination.

papers.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusionmodels generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Underteacher forcing, strongtemporal redundancymay allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to modelvisual evolution. We introduceFuture Chunk Prediction(FCP), an auxiliary objective jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising that predicts temporally separated chunks without access to the intervening visual context. Drawing supervision directly from training videos, FCP requires no additional pretrained visual encoder and leaves autoregressive inference unchanged. Our method achieves superior physical plausibility over standard teacher-forced autoregressive training with a lower overall training compute budget, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of future-chunk supervision for modelingvisual evolution. Intriguingly, our visualizations suggest that FCP fosters a more structured representation space, which may be valuable for building autoregressiveworld models.

papers.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
papers.abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accuratemetric mapsthrough autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluatingvision-language model(VLM) agents onactive object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection,cross-view association,geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding anintersection-over-union(IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precisemetric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations throughactive perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.

papers.title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
papers.abstract: Looped language modelscan run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems. Forsequential state tracking, final-answer supervision does not specify how far each iteration should advance, and repeated updates can change the scale of therecurrent state. We introduceProgress-Aligned Recurrence(PAR), which trains the prediction at iteration k to match the state after the first k operations and rescalesrecurrent states to their first-iteration norms. On swap-S_5, a Qwen2.5-0.5B model trained on at most 32 moves achieves 95.5\% mean full-state accuracy at 512 moves, or 16times the training length, compared with 55.7\% reported for RLT and 0.8\% for explicit chain of thought on the same backbone. Controlled S_5 ablations show that removingnorm anchoringreduces the extrapolation factor from 16times to below 2.2times, and replacing progress-aligned targets with final-answer supervision reduces it to at most 8times. A learned completion readout selects when to answer without a supplied stopping depth. When intermediate labels are unavailable,prefix self-distillationinduces the correspondence from shorter problem prefixes using only final answers. The gains apply across sequential state-tracking tasks, establishing the task structure required fordepth extrapolation. These findings support training intermediate predictions and state scale together to make additional recurrent depth useful for longer problems.

papers.title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
papers.abstract: Despite substantial progress inDeep Search agents, their ability to conduct end-to-end research in real-world open Web environments remains insufficiently evaluated. Unlike static retrieval settings, information on the real-world Web is distributed across diverse sources, modalities, and heterogeneous formats, often involving complex interaction mechanisms that require agents to autonomously search for, access, and integrate relevant evidence during execution. To address this gap, we introduce theOpenDStask, designed to evaluate agents' ability to performmulti-step deep searchin the live, open Web. This task requires agents to autonomously explore the real Web, discover and connect relevant evidence from multiple independent sources throughWeb search,browser interaction, andevidence processing, and ultimately determine a unique factual answer. Building on this task formulation, we constructOpenDS-World, a benchmark comprising 200 challenging tasks spanning diverse information modalities, heterogeneous file formats, and interactive access requirements, with independent human verification to ensure evidence validity and answer uniqueness. We evaluate 12 frontier models under a unified tool environment and execution protocol. The best-performing model achieves 39.0% accuracy, while human evaluation across 1,000 independent attempts yields 21.1% accuracy. Further analyses of tool usage, search cost, termination behavior, and failure recovery reveal substantial differences in research strategies across models, as well as persistent challenges intool coordinationandlong-horizon search management.OpenDS-Worldprovides a unified evaluation platform for systematically assessing and advancing agents' autonomous deep search capabilities in real-world open Web environments.

papers.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. The scarcity of contact-richbimanual manipulationdata and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging. Therefore, we present 1) DONIC, the first generalist bimanual tracker jointly trained across operation categories and human-motion sources, together with 2) BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences spanning 229 objects and emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction, where reconstructed interactions are retargeted into robot references. DONIC combinesproximal policy optimizationwithbehavioral cloningin a feedback loop that recycles verified successful executions into training demonstrations. An object-centeredper-hand rewardmaintains object-motion feedback while supervising each hand according to its reference contact role.Clip-Centered Advantagesremove reference-dependent advantage offsets while preserving within-trajectory differences. Together, these designs enable one single policy to learn coordinated manipulation across heterogeneous references. Without finetuning, a single checkpoint achieves 86.79% success on unseen trajectories of training objects and 57.32% on held-out objects, surpassing the state-of-the-art bimanual tracking baselines by 77.36 and 45.73 percentage points.

papers.title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
papers.abstract: CanAI agentscarry out research onopen scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, abenchmarkthat provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write afollow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of afollow-up paperis challenging in general, using these conditions to form arubricmakes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer. We have nine frontier agents write 15 follow-ups each, spanningquantum computing,plasma physics,computational chemistry,materials science, andscientific machine learningdomains. None of the 135 submissions satisfies all the conditions, and 114 fail ourintegrity check, most often because the paper claims work that was never done or reports numbers that contradict the recorded evidence. Overall, agents readily produce papers that look like follow-ups, but none meets the standard of the domain scientist, leaving substantial headroom. Our code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. As these trajectories grow, key-value (KV) cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost. Trajectories can also exceed the LLM's maximum context length, requiring control over active cache growth. Prior work usescontext engineeringto reduce cache size by trimming or summarizing history. However, modifying the trajectory prefix invalidates subsequent cached states and triggers costly re-prefilling of retained context. Task accuracy can also suffer when too little context is retained to limit re-prefill costs. We proposecache engineeringas a new scheme. It allows agents to directly control their active KV cache without modifying the trajectory or re-prefilling retained context. Specifically, agents can proactively usedropto exclude selected cache from future attention andreposto adjust retained keys'position encodings. We formalize these cache operations and identifyhistory dependenceas a serving challenge: identical token sequences can yield different cache states under different cache operation sequences, makingprefix matchinginsufficient for correct cache reuse. Thus, we co-design theAKV serving engine. It provides a stateless interface compatible with existing serving APIs, while internally managing stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration. Experiments show that a tool-responserolling-drop cache policyimproves average benchmark scores by 1.7 points and reduces average cost by 27.7%, compared with conventional threshold-triggered summarization. With AKV, it achieves up to 1.2x the output throughput and a 1.5x speedup in P95 request latency.Recursive self-improvementof cache policies further reduces cost by 7.1% over expert design. Our code is at https://github.com/thu-nics/AKV.

papers.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
papers.abstract: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the firstegocentric loco-manipulationworld foundation modelspanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unifiedkinematic representationencodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specificforward kinematicswith extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across fivecross-embodimentbenchmarks (DreamDojo, Ψ_0, ω-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation,model-based planning, andworld-action modelingfurther demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.
